 --> Diwali 2026 Date: Deepawali complete festival calendar with dates, Muhurat and significance
 Diwali 2026 will be celebrated from November 5 to 11. Check the complete Deepawali calendar, important festival dates, Lakshmi Puja muhurat and rituals.

 Diwali 2026 Date: Deepawali complete festival calendar with dates, Muhurat and significance (image: canva) Diwali 2026 runs from November 5 to November 11.
 Main Lakshmi Puja is scheduled for November 8, 2026.
 Festivals include Dhanteras, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.

 Diwali 2026 will be celebrated over several days, with each occasion carrying its own religious significance, rituals and traditions. Also known as Deepawali or Deepavali, the festival is associated with the worship of Goddess Lakshmi, the lighting of diyas, family gatherings and the victory of good over evil. The celebrations traditionally begin with Govatsa Dwadashi in some regions and continue through Dhanteras, Kali Chaudas, Narak Chaturdashi and Lakshmi Puja. The festivities conclude with Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj.
 In 2026, the festival calendar provided lists celebrations from November 5 to November 11. However, there is an important date discrepancy in the supplied calendar: it lists Lakshmi Puja on November 8, while November 9 is marked as Diwali Snan on Amavasya. Since the main Diwali Lakshmi Puja is traditionally observed on the Amavasya evening, the dates and associated muhurat should be checked against a verified regional Panchang before publication.
 Diwali 2026: Complete festival calendar and important dates 
 Here is the seven-day festival schedule, from Govatsa Dwadashi to Bhai Dooj, based on the dates in the supplied calendar.
 Festival Date and Time 
 Govatsa Dwadashi (Vasu Baras) Thursday, November 5, 2026 
 Dhanteras, Dhanvantari Trayodashi, Yama Deepam Friday, November 6, 2026 
 Kali Chaudas, Hanuman Puja Saturday, November 7, 2026 
 Narak Chaturdashi, Diwali, Lakshmi Puja, Kali Puja Sunday, November 8, 2026 
 Diwali Snan, Diwali Devpuja Monday, November 9, 2026 
 Govardhan Puja, Annakut, Bali Pratipada, Gujarati New Year Tuesday, November 10, 2026 
 Bhai Dooj, Bhau Beej, Chitragupta Puja Wednesday, November 11, 2026 
 The main Lakshmi Puja and Diwali celebrations fall on Sunday, November 8, 2026 . Although Amavasya continues until the following day, the new moon tithi prevails during the evening of November 8, which determines the date of Lakshmi Puja.
 Diwali 2026 Lakshmi puja muhurat 
 Lakshmi Puja is traditionally performed during Pradosh Kaal, the period after sunset. The Amavasya tithi must prevail during this evening period for the main Diwali worship. According to Drik Panchang, the Lakshmi Puja muhurat for New Delhi on November 8, 2026, is:
 Event Date and Time 
 Lakshmi puja Sunday, November 8, 2026 
 Lakshmi puja muhurat 5:54 PM – 7:50 PM 
 The muhurat varies by city because sunset and local Panchang calculations differ. Check the timings for your location before performing the puja.
 Diwali 2026: Significance of each festival day 
 1. Govatsa Dwadashi: November 5 
 Govatsa Dwadashi, also known as Vasu Baras, marks the beginning of Diwali celebrations in several parts of India, particularly Maharashtra. Cows and calves are worshipped on this day as symbols of nourishment, prosperity and motherhood. Devotees offer prayers and express gratitude for the important role of cattle in traditional agricultural life.
 2. Dhanteras: November 6 
 Dhanteras, also known as Dhantrayodashi or Dhanvantari Trayodashi, is dedicated to wealth, health and prosperity. Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Kuber are worshipped on this occasion. Many families consider it auspicious to purchase gold, silver, utensils and other household items. Lighting a lamp in the evening, known as Yama Deepam, is another important tradition associated with the day.
 3. Kali Chaudas: November 7 
 Kali Chaudas is observed on the day before the main Diwali celebrations in several regions. It is also known as Narak Chaturdashi in some traditions, although the two observances can fall on different dates depending on regional customs and the Panchang. Devotees worship Goddess Kali and Lord Hanuman, seeking protection from negative forces and obstacles. Rituals and prayers vary across communities.
 4. Narak Chaturdashi and Lakshmi Puja: November 8 
 Narak Chaturdashi, also called Choti Diwali, is associated with the victory of Lord Krishna over the demon Narakasura. The occasion symbolises the triumph of good over evil. The evening of November 8 is also the main Diwali celebration in 2026. Families light diyas, decorate their homes, exchange sweets and worship Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Ganesha.
 Lakshmi Puja is considered the most important ritual of Diwali. Devotees pray for wealth, happiness, peace and prosperity. Kali Puja, Chopda Puja and Sharda Puja are also observed by different communities.
 5. Diwali Snan and Devpuja: November 9 
 The day after the main Diwali evening is marked as Diwali Snan and Devpuja in the supplied calendar. Amavasya continues until around midday on November 9, after which the Pratipada tithi begins. Devotees follow their family and regional traditions for ritual bathing, prayers and other religious observances.
 6. Govardhan Puja: November 10 
 Govardhan Puja, also known as Annakut, commemorates Lord Krishna's protection of the people of Vrindavan by lifting Govardhan Hill. Devotees prepare a variety of food offerings, arrange them as Annakut and offer prayers to Lord Krishna. The festival also highlights gratitude towards nature and the importance of agriculture and cattle.
 Bali Pratipada and the Gujarati New Year are also observed around this time in several communities.
 7. Bhai Dooj: November 11 
 Bhai Dooj, also known as Bhau Beej or Yama Dwitiya, celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters apply a ceremonial tilak on their brothers' foreheads and pray for their long lives, health and happiness. Brothers, in turn, offer gifts and reaffirm their affection and support. Chitragupta Puja is also observed by some communities on this day.
 Why is goddess Lakshmi worshipped during Diwali? 
 Goddess Lakshmi is regarded as the deity of wealth, prosperity and good fortune. Her worship is central to Diwali celebrations, particularly among families and business communities. The main Lakshmi Puja takes place on Kartik Amavasya. Homes and workplaces are cleaned and decorated before the evening rituals, while diyas are lit to welcome prosperity and positivity.
 Many traditional business families also perform Chopda Puja, during which new account books, known as Bahi-Khate, are worshipped. Pens and inkpots, traditionally called Lekhani and Davat, are also included in certain rituals. Goddess Saraswati is worshipped for knowledge and wisdom, while Goddess Kali is associated with the protection and removal of negative forces.
 Why is Pradosh Kaal important for Diwali lakshmi puja? 
 Pradosh Kaal refers to the period shortly after sunset and is considered especially auspicious for Diwali Lakshmi Puja. The main criterion for choosing the Diwali Puja date is the presence of Amavasya tithi during Pradosh Kaal. Even if Amavasya continues into the following morning, the evening on which it coincides with Pradosh Kaal is generally considered the appropriate time for the main Lakshmi Puja.
 This is why Diwali 2026 is observed on November 8, even though Amavasya continues into November 9.
